title: 68901 MFP
body:
The 68901 MFP Is the [[PIC]] On the 68k.
The 68901 is smart enough for vector transfer.

**Multi-Function Peripheral**, and the name is honest: it is a [[PIC]], four timers, a
[[UART]], and some general-purpose I/O lines in one package. The interrupt controller part is
what matters here.

Sixteen interrupt sources funnel into one line to the [[CPU]]. The MFP prioritises them, and
because it does vector transfer it supplies the vector number itself rather than making the
processor guess, so each source can have its own [[ISRs|ISR]] with no polling of "who
interrupted me". Each source has a mask bit (do not bother me) and an enable bit, so the
[[Kernel]] can turn individual devices off without raising the whole
[[Interrupt Mask|interrupt level]].

Its timers are how the machine gets a periodic tick, which is what any preemptive scheduler
in [[OPERATING SYSTEMS]] needs to exist.

[[Interrupts]] · [[Priority Encoder]] · [[6850 ACIA]] · [[GLUE]] · [[COMPUTING MACHINERY 2]]
